title: Amazon Science introduces priming method for hybrid AI model architectures
excerpt: The new approach reduces pretraining costs for hybrid models by over 99 percent by leveraging pretrained Transformer weights.
bodyHtml:
Amazon Science announced on October 12, 2026, a method called priming that allows developers to change an AI model's architecture without retraining from scratch. The technique reuses pretrained Transformer weights to build hybrid models, which combine different methods to balance memory, speed, and quality.

According to the paper, priming reduces pretraining costs for hybrid architectures by more than 99 percent, saving trillions of tokens and hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours. The method works across Transformer families including Qwen, Llama, and Mistral, as well as different model classes and scales.

The team released a collection of primed hybrid models at the eight-billion-parameter and 32-billion-parameter scales. These releases include training code, optimized kernels, and a vLLM-serving plugin under the Apache 2.0 License.
topic: Can we change an AI model’s architecture without retraining it from scratch?
